citations.authors: Sandefer R, Marc D, Mancilla D, Hamada D
citations.title: AHIMA Workforce Study: Health Information Professionals in the Era of Big Data
citations.what_it_says: Documents RHIA placement into HIM management, compliance, and emerging analytics roles, with the credential viewed as standard for HIM department leadership.

citations.authors: Marc DT, Robertson J, Gordon L, Green-Lawson Z, Dover K
citations.title: Health Information Management Workforce: Looking Forward to 2030
citations.what_it_says: Projects sustained employer demand for RHIA-credentialed leaders in data governance, informatics, and revenue cycle, with salary growth concentrated at director level.

citations.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical Records and Health Information Specialists
citations.what_it_says: Reports median pay around $48K for the broader occupation with bachelor's-prepared RHIAs concentrated in management roles paying substantially more and 8% projected growth through 2032.

citations.authors: Fenton SH, Low S, Abrams KJ, Butler-Henderson K
citations.title: Competencies Required for the Health Informatics Workforce
citations.what_it_says: Maps RHIA curriculum to informatics competencies, showing strength in data governance and classification but gaps in programming and analytics that limit fit for vendor technical roles.

citations.authors: Watzlaf VJM, Garner J, Lipinski K, Ruben D, Firouzan P
citations.title: An Evaluation of the Rigor of the RHIA Certification Examination
citations.what_it_says: Confirms RHIA is a bachelor's-gated credential with exam content centered on HIM operations, supporting its narrow transition fit outside HIM-trained candidates.

citations.authors: Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology
citations.title: ONC Health IT Workforce Development Program: Evaluation Report
citations.what_it_says: Identifies HIM-credentialed (including RHIA) professionals as a primary pipeline for hospital and payer informatics roles, though notes EHR vendor analyst roles preferentially recruit clinical-background candidates.
